concurrency_primitives: goroutines + sync.WaitGroup + sync.Mutex: 2 goroutines load 2 CSVs (loader.go:55-73); 2 goroutines append into a single mutex-guarded index (joiner.go:48-70); analysis sequential; no channels, no worker pool
design_patterns: Strategy (RecordParser interface with two parsers), trivial Factory constructors, ordered pipeline in main()
questions: Neighborhood burden ranking by combined 311 + crime volume
Neighborhoods with both burglaries and vacant-property 311 reports
overview: Small, tidy single-package Go program split into six focused files with a genuine Strategy interface for parsers and a mutex-guarded neighborhood index. Parsing is positional and records are boxed as interface{}, so it only works on the two hand-built CSVs it ships with. No tests; README is accurate and honest about the data.
stakeholder_value: No actionable value: all five answers are computed over twelve invented rows, and Q2 depends on literal values (CrimeCode 'BURGLARY', SRType 'VACANT') that never occur in real Open Baltimore data. Q5 (311-per-crime ratio) is a reasonable idea that could be informative on real data; Q4 is single-dataset.
issues: Fully simulated data: 6+6 hand-built rows; headers (SRNumber, CrimeCode=BURGLARY) do not match Open Baltimore schemas despite README claim
No download script, URL, or generator for real data
Positional column parsing and hard-coded category literals would break on real exports
Token concurrency; join serialized under a single mutex; analysis sequential
No tests; interface{} boxing with type assertions; unused requests.csv at repo root
rationale: Full build credit and partial architecture credit for a clean, well-organized Go program that compiles and runs first try. Zero real-data credit because both datasets are invented, token concurrency credit, and low stakeholder/run credit because the answers are vacuous and partly depend on nonexistent values. Total 45/100, F.
